note: Literature explicitly documents nystagmus occurring in both the severe neonatal-onset form and the milder childhood-onset spastic ataxia spectrum.

evidence.text: GeneReviews reports neonatal-onset nystagmus at the severe end of the spectrum, as well as nystagmus among the cerebellar findings at the milder end of the spastic ataxia spectrum.

source.title: NKX6-2-related disorder
source.quote: At the severe end of the spectrum is neonatal-onset nystagmus, severe spastic tetraplegia with joint contractures and scoliosis... At the milder end of the spectrum is normal achievement of early motor milestones in the first year of life followed by slowly progressive complex spastic ataxia with pyramidal findings... and cerebellar findings (nystagmus, extraocular movement disorder, dysarthria, titubation, and ataxia)

evidence.text: Phenotypes across the spectrum from childhood-onset milder motor presentation to severe neonatal onset can present without overt hypomyelination, with early nystagmus and cerebellar ataxia being key clinical features.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: phenotypes with epilepsy in the absence of overt hypomyelination and diffuse hypomyelination without seizures can occur. Conclusions: NKX6-2 mutations should be considered in patients with autosomal recessive, very early onset of nystagmus, cerebellar ataxia with hypotonia that rapidly progresses to spasticity
